title: Business Operations and HR Coordinator
description:
My client is a school based just outside Hastings who is looking to bring in an experienced Business Operations and HR Coordinator to join the team during a sustained period of growth.
Reporting directly to the Bursar, this role will be responsible for supporting the HR function in day-to-day activities including working with and giving guidance to all staff.

The Business Operations and HR Coordinator is responsible for supporting the efficient day-to-day running of the school's operations while coordinating key Human Resources functions. The role provides comprehensive administrative support across HR, operational management, compliance, health and safety, and facilities coordination, ensuring that systems, processes, and records are maintained to the highest standards.

The ideal candidate will have at least 2 years HR experience and be actively studying towards there CIPD qualifications. It is imperative that you have strong communication and administration skills, HR systems experience and excellent attention to detail.

You must have access to your own transport due to the location of this role.

Farrer Barnes Ltd does not discriminate on the grounds of age, race, gender, disability, creed or sexual orientation and complies with all relevant UK legislation. Farrer Barnes Ltd acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers.

title: HR Administrator
description:
What you'll be doing:
Southdown is the largest not-for-profit provider of care, support and housing in Sussex. We've been helping people access stable accommodation, mental health and care services since 1972, and today more than 900 people are part of our team.

As an HR Administrator (known internally as a People Services Administrator), you'll join our People Services team, providing high-quality administrative support across the employee lifecycle. This includes recruitment and onboarding, absence management, training, employee relations and offboarding.

You'll be a key point of support for colleagues and managers, helping to ensure our People processes are accurate, responsive and run smoothly. You'll need to be organised, comfortable managing a varied workload and confident working with detailed and confidential information.

This is an exciting time to join us as we continue to develop and improve our People Services function, including the introduction of a new HR ticketing system. If you're looking for a varied role where no two days are quite the same, and where you can make a real contribution to the experience of our colleagues, we'd love to hear from you.

We welcome applications from people with experience in roles such as HR Administrator, People Administrator, Recruitment Administrator, Onboarding Administrator, HR Coordinator, HR Services Administrator or similar People/HR support roles.

Perks and benefits:
- Health cost cash-back scheme: access to our health insurance scheme which covers dental, optical, physical therapies and other medical treatments with the option to add greater levels of cover.
- Interest-free loans: assistance with larger costs that arise such as tenancy deposits, season travel tickets or buying a car.
- Access to the Easit Network: discounts and incentives on train, bus and car journeys such as 15% off eligible daily and season rail tickets.
- Blue Light card: access to discount services for the social care sector with savings across thousands of online shops, restaurants, and high-street vendors.
- Free advice and counselling service: confidential emotional support and practical guidance from our independent telephone service.
- 25 days paid holiday plus bank holidays.

Working arrangements
This is a 37 hours per week role, working Monday to Thursday, 9.00am to 5.00pm, and Friday, 9.00am to 4.30pm. The role is offered on a hybrid basis, with a minimum of two days each week in our Lewes office.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

What you'll need for the role:
- Previous experience working in an HR or People Services team
- Knowledge of UK employment law, GDPR and best HR practices
- Experience in HR systems including HR Information Systems (HRIS), Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), and Learning Management Systems platforms (LMS).
- Knowledge of Recruitment lifecycle, onboarding compliance, and employment checks.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines
- Good written and verbal communication skills and a helpful, customer-focused approach

What would be nice:
- CIPD Level 3 qualification (or working towards it)

Training:
Our award-winning in-house training team will help you to gain valuable qualifications, continually develop your skills and build a great career with the largest provider of housing, care and support in Sussex.

How to apply:
Please click on the 'Apply Now' button and fill out our simple one-page application form.

Please note, if we receive a large number of applications then this position may close before the advertised application closing date. We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.

title: Senior HR Administrator
description:
As a Senior HR Administrator in Littlehampton, you'll take care of the day-to-day running of HR processes in the professional services industry. Your role will help ensure everything runs smoothly by managing key administrative tasks and supporting the HR function.

Client Details
- This role is based within the professional services industry in Littlehampton.
- Demonstrate high degree of integrity and maintain confidentiality.
- Demonstrate basic understanding of the business, industry, clients, and business processes of assigned business.
- Be proficient at providing instruction/information to employees in the use of HR programs, tools, services.
- Demonstrate proficiency in conducting HR analytics (accurately analyses data, identifies trends and presents in a clear and logical manner that allows users to quickly interpret and identify appropriate action).
- Takes personal accountability & initiative - identifies issues (pro-active); take action to resolve (can-do); go beyond what is required (ownership).
- Strong interpersonal skills.
- Ability to prioritise.

Description
- Onboard new clients and establish their HR policies and systems.
- Prepare HR documents such as employment contracts and new hire guides.
- Co-ordinate induction sessions and ensure all documentation is completed, recorded, and communicated effectively.
- Review and update company policies.
- Liaise with external partners such as Occupational Health, HRIS providers and legal compliance.
- Create regular reports and presentations on HR metrics (e.g. turnover rates, stability, absence).
- Proactively manage varied HR Information systems, updating records in a timely manner (e.g. starters, leavers, maternity, holiday).
- Monitor and manage client HR in-boxes, responding where appropriate and escalating to HR Advisors where needed.
- Support HR Advisors and HRBPs by ensuring all disciplinary, grievance, absence and performance management cases and outcomes have been captured, recorded and logged in the relevant HRIS
- Ensure the accurate recording and archiving of all employees related documents and correspondence in line with GDPR and Data Protection legislation.
- Update the HR System with sickness reasons and ensure medical certificates and return to work interview forms are received and filed.
- Process leavers on the HR System and ensure all associated paperwork is actioned and distributed as required.
- Provide timely employment references when requested in accordance with policy.
- Administer the maternity process by issuing maternity information and processing paperwork/updating the HR System.
- Ensure the client Organisation charts are kept up to date with leavers and staff changes.
- Answer phone & email queries about HR admin related activities.
- Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
- Assist payroll providers by providing relevant employee information (e.g. leave, absence, sick days and work schedules).
- Provide accurate and timely administration support to our team and clients.
- Ensure all correspondence are prepared to a high standard with a 'right first time' approach to detail.
- Participate in HR projects
- Act as first line advisory support to clients for employment enquiries and for direct client relationships where assigned.

Profile

A successful Senior HR Administrator should have:
- CIPD qualified to at least level 5 or equivalent occupational qualifications.
- Comprehensive and up to date knowledge of relevant ER and HR related legislation.
- 3 years of experience within a relevant HR role.
- Excellent customer service skills.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Can flex communication style according to listener / audience.
- Loves working as part of a team but also self-motivated and disciplined.
- Analytical and problem-solving abilities.
- Comprehensive understanding of HR legal requirements and best practices.
- Excellent knowledge of employment contracts and terms and the application of typical HR processes.

Job Offer
- An hourly rate of £16.00 to £18.00, dependent on the level of experience.
- Monday to Friday 9:00am until 5:00pm, 30 minutes for lunch
- 2 days a week in office, 3 days WFH
- Initial 6 week assignment

If you're interested in this role, apply now.
